judgment.rationale: Both are same-grain Knowledge Objectives at the same P2 coordinate (rank 1) under Unit 8 'Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 1000 Frw' / Key Unit Competence on counting and exchanging currency. The first requires identifying and listing the values of Rwandan denominations from 1Frw to 1000Frw (LCs: 'identify/list the value of Rwandan currency from 1Frw to 1000Frw'); the second requires explaining how to add, subtract, multiply and divide Rwandan currency (LCs for each operation). Their content differs substantively: the second SFI is recognition-level work ('Identify and extend simple repeating number patterns within the range of 0 to 99', LCs 'identify...' and 'extend simple repeating number patterns 0-99'), while the first requires learners to generate a pattern by applying an operation rule ('Use addition or substraction to form a number pattern', LCs 'use addition to form a number pattern' / 'use subtraction to form a number pattern'). Being able to identify and continue an existing repeating pattern plausibly supports success in constructing patterns through addition or subtraction, so the developmental direction runs second_to_first rather than the reverse. Shared parent Key Unit Competence, same table row, page 45 proximity and the thin token overlap ('number', 'to') were treated as nomination signals only. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so this direction rests on the visible statement and LC text; confidence is accordingly moderate.
